The European Commission is also in “close contact” with France’s ARCOM media regulator to ensure social media and video-sharing platforms enforce digital content rules against information manipulation and incitement to violence.
“When online platforms are becoming aware or have a suspicion of a criminal offence that may occur, they have to proactively enforce and inform national authorities,” EU spokesman Thomas Regnier said.
Regnier added that the commission was “ready to assist and to support the national authorities”.
The unrest followed weeks of student demonstrations, some of which were accompanied by street violence. The protests have added to pressure on the government amid a weak economy and rising public debt, six months ahead of the next presidential election.

Italian police detain hundreds as stores looted in weekend unrest in Milan
MILAN – Italian police detained 271 young people during unrest in Milan on Oct 18, the authorities said, after a second day of protests over poor public services and rising costs that saw demonstrators clash with officers, loot stores and vandalise property.
Police in riot gear fired tear gas and water cannon as several hundred hooded protesters set bins ablaze and looted stores, including sports retailers Decathlon and Arc’teryx and phone store Vodafone in the city centre, according to TV footage.
Of those taken to police stations, 32 were arrested, including 23 minors and 13 foreign nationals, the police said on Oct 19. A further 28 people were reported to judicial authorities.
The unrest followed similar clashes on Oct 17 in northern cities, including Milan, Bologna, Brescia, Bergamo and Turin, where 28 protesters were arrested, according to a police report released on Oct 18.
The disturbances echoed unrest in neighbouring France, where hundreds of thousands of people angered by rising living costs and declining public services took to the streets on Oct 17 in some of the country’s most violent protests in years.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, who faces an election in 2027, condemned the violence and announced a government meeting on Oct 19 to discuss how to address the situation. REUTERS

Mitsubishi to Reopen Shipbuilding Yard in Tamano Amid Rising Orders
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
11:50:37 UTC
20:50:37 KST

Mitsubishi Heavy Industries plans to resume operations at its shipbuilding slipway in Tamano, Okayama Prefecture, in fiscal year 2027.
The Japanese outlet Nikkei reported this.
The company aims to expand its warship-building capacity amid rising defense spending in Japan and growing opportunities to export military equipment.
In particular, the company is considering using the slipway to build a new support vessel for the Japan Ministry of Defense.
Mitsubishi Heavy Industries also plans to increase the number of employees involved in shipbuilding.
The slipway is at Maritime Systems’ main plant in Tamano, a subsidiary of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. The facility was previously owned by Mitsui Shipbuilding, now known as Mitsui E&S.
In 2021, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries took over the company’s shipbuilding business after it exited the sector.
Militarnyi previously reported that the Chief of the Royal New Zealand Navy had visited the Japanese Ministry of Defense and expressed interest in acquiring Japanese frigates to modernize the country’s surface fleet.
Construction of New FFM Frigates
One of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries’ main areas of activity is the construction of Mogami-class frigates. In August 2025, Australia selected an upgraded version of the vessel to modernize its navy.
On April 18, 2026, the parties signed a contract to build the first three frigates.
Japan has also started procuring next-generation frigates under the New FFM program, known as the 06FFM. The country plans to acquire a total of 12 such vessels for the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force. The plan calls for building up to two frigates per year, which will require expanding shipbuilding capacity.
To avoid delays from occupied dry docks and slipways, the company plans to concentrate frigate construction at Japan’s main shipyards.
Meanwhile, the company plans to shift construction of other vessel types, including support ships, to secondary production facilities.

UK faces 'economic catastrophe, moral failure' over youth unemployment: Premier
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
11:49:05 UTC
20:49:05 KST

Aysu Bicer
19 October 2026•Update: 19 October 2026
The UK faces an "economic catastrophe and moral failure" as nearly 1 million young people remain outside education, employment or training, Prime Minister Andy Burnham warned Monday.
Writing in The Times newspaper, Burnham called on the government to "invest in the success of our young people" rather than "pay for failure through the benefits system."
"Benefits will become the backstop, not the starting point," he wrote in an opinion article published Monday.
Burnham also said a long-awaited review of young people and work would be published next month, pledging to take its recommendations "seriously."
According to the latest data from the Office for National Statistics, nearly 1 million people aged 16 to 24 in the UK are not in education, employment or training.
Around 39% of them are unemployed, while the remaining 61% are economically inactive, meaning they are not seeking work, the figures showed.
Burnham attributed the crisis to several factors, including two years of COVID-19 lockdowns, social media, an education system focused on university education, limited job opportunities and failures by previous governments.
He argued that social media erodes young people's "confidence and sense of belonging."
"This is an economic catastrophe and a moral failure. And it must change," he wrote.
Burnham criticized the current welfare system, arguing that it often provides financial support without offering young people a route into employment.
"Today, the welfare system provides an assessment, a payment and, after that, goodbye," he wrote.
"Too often there is no support, no offer of skills and no opportunity to get a job."
He said the government's approach should shift toward identifying young people's ambitions and providing the assistance needed to achieve them, rather than beginning with an assessment of benefit entitlement.
"The safety net will always be there for those who cannot work. But if someone can work with the right help, the government has a duty to do everything in its power to make that happen," Burnham said.

Sudanese army says it repelled RSF ground attack in Blue Nile, intercepted drones over Khartoum
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
11:47:51 UTC
20:47:51 KST

Adel Abdel Rahim and Sahin Demir
19 October 2026•Update: 19 October 2026
The Sudanese army said Monday it had repelled a ground attack by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and its ally, the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N), in southeastern Blue Nile state, while its air defenses intercepted a drone attack east of the capital Khartoum.
In a statement, the army’s 14th Infantry Division said its forces thwarted an attack by the RSF and SPLM-N on the Al-Baraka area in the southern sector of Blue Nile state.
The division said its troops inflicted heavy casualties and equipment losses on the attacking forces, preventing them from advancing toward army positions.
It added that several military vehicles were destroyed and the attackers were forced to retreat under heavy fire.
The division said the operation demonstrated the army’s readiness to respond to any hostile movements threatening its positions or the security of civilians and their property.
There was no immediate comment from the RSF or SPLM-N on the army’s claims.
Blue Nile state has witnessed escalating military tensions in recent weeks following attacks by the RSF and SPLM-N on several areas.
 
Drone attack
In a separate development, military sources told Anadolu that army air defenses intercepted an RSF drone attack east of Khartoum on Monday, near Khartoum International Airport.
The sources said all attacking drones were shot down but did not specify their number.
Witnesses also told Anadolu that explosions were heard in the skies over eastern Khartoum on Monday morning.
Videos circulated on social media showed a drone flying over the Sudanese capital the same day.
There was no immediate comment from Sudanese authorities or the RSF on the reported drone attack.
On May 4, Sudan’s Information Ministry reported that a site within Khartoum International Airport had been targeted by a drone, without causing casualties or material damage.
Sudanese authorities and human rights organizations have accused the RSF of targeting civilian facilities. The group rarely comments on such accusations but maintains that it works to protect civilians.
Since April 2023, the Sudanese army and RSF have been engaged in a war that erupted over disagreements concerning the integration of the paramilitary group into the country’s military.
The conflict has killed tens of thousands of people and displaced around 13 million, while worsening famine and humanitarian conditions in what has become one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises.

Lebanon: end of the joint visit by M. Jean-Noël Barrot, Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs, and Mme Alice Rufo, Minister Delegate attached to the Minister for the Armed Forces and Veterans International cooperation Defence and security Communiqué On : October 18th 2026 M. Jean-Noël Barrot, Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs, and Mme Alice Rufo, Minister Delegate attached to the Minister for the Armed Forces and Veterans, visited Lebanon on 17 and 18 October. They had meetings with the President of the Lebanese Republic, Mr Joseph Aoun; the Prime Minister, Mr Nawaf Salam; the President of the Chamber of Deputies, Mr Nabih Berri; and the Army Commander-in-Chief, General Haykal. Finally, the Minister Delegate had a meeting with the Minister of National Defence, Mr Michel Menassa. The ministers reaffirmed France’s wholehearted support for the Lebanese authorities in their efforts to restore sovereignty, stability and functioning institutions throughout Lebanon’s territory and in the long term. In this regard, they emphasized the importance of strengthening the Lebanese Armed Forces and effectively implementing the state monopoly on weapons, and France’s readiness to contribute to this goal. They reiterated the need for the ceasefire to be observed, civilians and infrastructure to be protected and Lebanon’s territorial integrity to be respected. They reaffirmed France’s support for the efforts being made by the Lebanese authorities to achieve a lasting political solution, in the interests of Lebanon’s and the region’s stability. With the mandate of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon due to be completed at the end of the year, the ministers stressed the need to create an international architecture to back Lebanon’s sovereignty – something essential in order to avoid a security vacuum and support the redeployment of the Lebanese Armed Forces and therefore the implementation of the Framework Agreement of 26 June 2026 and United Nations Security Council Resolution 1701. The ministers recalled that France is ready to play its full part in this. Together with the Lebanese authorities, they welcomed the European Union’s adoption on 12 October of the decision establishing the EU Support Mission to Lebanon, whose remit is to serve as a significant element in this new architecture. Koretsky: government to review draft deferral rules due to sharp rise in deferred workers
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
14:46:54 EEST
20:46:54 KST

The Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine has decided to review the rules and criteria for the deferral procedure for draft-eligible employees, as the monthly volume of military draft deferrals has reached tens of thousands of people and is growing at an unsustainable rate, Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky reported in an interview with BBC News Ukraine.
"Statistics over the last 6–8 months show a monthly deferral rate in the tens of thousands. And it is growing at an incredible pace. If this dynamic continues, soon absolutely everyone will be deferred. Everyone says that today obtaining a deferral to secure peace of mind from mobilization has become significantly easier. Therefore, to at least stop this dynamic, which has taken on a very negative trend, and to avoid abuse and manipulation within the system, we are proposing a revision of the rules," the head of government stated.
The prime minister denied claims that the government halted the decision to change the rules due to scandal or public criticism, dismissing such assertions as manipulation. According to him, the top priority remains the country's defense capability and meeting the General Staff's mobilization needs for troop rotations, as well as replacing the wounded and fallen.
Koretsky emphasized that the key objective of the updated mechanism is to minimize abuses where companies are created under the guise of critically important enterprises for mass employee deferrals despite not being involved in executing vital tasks. Meanwhile, the two core criteria for determining an enterprise's critical status must remain defense capability and state life support.
"Criticality comes down to two main points: defense capability and state life support. Therefore, step number one is to define what is truly critical, and there are zero questions about those. Nothing to worry about. Those who should worry are those who set up a company that produces, say, two drones a year, yet deferred hundreds of people as employees," the prime minister noted.
Speaking about the possible implementation of so-called "economic deferral," the prime minister remarked that high salary levels and an absence of tax debts are not synonymous with a company's critical importance to the state during wartime, and also raise questions of fairness regarding service members on the front lines.
The head of government expressed hope that the final details of the updated deferral system will be agreed upon and refined over the course of the current week. According to him, the changes will not harm strategic sectors, particularly energy ahead of the winter period.
As reported, news of changes to the deferral procedure emerged on October 12, when MP Yaroslav Zheleznyak cited personal sources regarding the revisions. It was later revealed that the government had approved a draft resolution subject to a five-day revision of certain provisions. However, the resolution itself was not published on the Cabinet website.
Business associations subsequently reported that they did not support the draft resolution and that the government had failed to conduct consultations regarding possible changes, urging an open discussion of the document's provisions and a dialogue with the government and relevant authorities. In particular, joint appeals were issued by the Union of Ukrainian Entrepreneurs (SUP), the European Business Association (EBA), the Federation of Employers of Ukraine (FRU), the Economic Expert Platform (comprising 16 analytical organizations), the National Association of Extractive Industry of Ukraine (NAEIU), Executive Secretary of the Ukrainian Association of Critical Infrastructure Operators (UACIO) Ruslan Holub, Tech Forces of Ukraine (TSU), the Armorers Council (132 defense organizations), the National Association of Ukrainian Defense Industries (NAUDI), volunteer organizations assisting the military, and the Union of Dairy Enterprises.
According to the draft Cabinet resolution available to Interfax-Ukraine, the document provides for the establishment of a Coordination Center as a consultative and advisory body to the Cabinet, serving as an additional clearance stage before decisions are made by line ministries regarding enterprise criticality designations.
The draft also envisages lowering the deferral quota limit from 100% to 85% for employees of defense-industrial complex (DIC) enterprises, critical companies, and contractors in the fuel and energy sector that ensure the uninterrupted operation of the power system and gas transmission network, alongside reducing the normative deferral quota for certain categories of institutions from 75% to 60%. Furthermore, increasing deferral limits beyond 50% would be possible exclusively on the basis of recommendations from the Coordination Center.
In addition, the draft introduces a mandatory clearance stage through this center prior to decisions being made by line ministries on defining enterprises as critically important.
It also regulates decision-making procedures by government bodies based on the Coordination Center's recommendations within 3 business days. According to an evaluation by the Ministry of Finance, the draft resolution was approved without objections, as its implementation does not require additional expenditures from the state budget and will not impact current-period budget indicators.

Exclusive: Breakthrough expected in US-Iran mediation efforts
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
11:45:24 UTC
20:45:24 KST

Breadcrumb
Exclusive: Breakthrough expected in US-Iran mediation efforts this week
A breakthrough in mediation efforts between the United States and Iran is expected to be announced this week, sources familiar with the negotiations told The New Arab on Monday, as Qatar and Pakistan continue diplomatic efforts to prevent a renewed war between Washington and Tehran.
Senior sources familiar with the mediation efforts, speaking to The New Arab on condition of anonymity, said negotiations were continuing to narrow differences and encourage mutual concessions aimed at preventing another military confrontation.
Despite ongoing threats exchanged between Washington and Tehran, and concerns that the war with Iran could resume after the US midterm elections on 3 November, the sources ruled out an immediate escalation in the region.
The anticipated breakthrough comes amid mounting tensions over Iran's nuclear programme, the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz and US demands for Tehran to curb its uranium enrichment capabilities.
On Saturday evening, US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth warned that Iran would face "destruction" unless it abandoned its nuclear ambitions at the negotiating table.
Speaking at the University of Tennessee in Knoxville, Hegseth accused Iran of building a "large arsenal" of conventional missiles and attempting to pursue a strategy similar to that of North Korea.
Meanwhile, US embassies across the region have warned of the possibility of rapidly developing security threats, including potential attacks by Iran and its regional allies.
Iran accuses Netanyahu of pushing for another war
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Sunday accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of attempting to drag the United States into another war with Tehran to avoid imprisonment.
Responding to remarks made by Netanyahu about Iran, Araghchi wrote on X that the Israeli leader was "dragging the United States into a new war to avoid going to prison", while disregarding the potential consequences for Israel and the US president.
The Iranian foreign minister also reiterated Tehran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, provided Washington meets several Iranian demands.
These include lifting the blockade on Iranian ports, easing restrictions on Iranian oil exports and halting hostilities across regional fronts.
Araghchi said Tehran had received US feedback on the proposal and was reviewing it, although significant disagreements continued to obstruct progress.
According to Reuters, one of the main sticking points remains Washington's insistence on placing Iran's nuclear programme at the centre of negotiations, including demands for substantial reductions in Tehran's uranium enrichment capabilities.
Iran, however, wants to prioritise reopening the Strait of Hormuz and addressing the economic and security restrictions imposed on the country.
Qatar and Pakistan intensify mediation efforts
Qatar and Pakistan have continued diplomatic efforts to bridge differences between Washington and Tehran, although political and security obstacles have so far prevented an agreement that could end the confrontation and restore regional stability.
The talks come amid growing concerns over the consequences of the Strait of Hormuz remaining closed, with disruptions to shipping and global energy supplies adding urgency to efforts to reach a settlement.
Iran's ISNA news agency reported on Sunday that Pakistan's army chief, Asim Munir, could visit Tehran this week as part of ongoing cooperation between the two countries and discussions concerning regional developments and US-Iran negotiations.
The Strait of Hormuz remains one of the central issues in the crisis because of its strategic importance to global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments.
Reopening the waterway could serve not only as a measure to restore maritime traffic but also as an initial confidence-building step towards reducing tensions and restarting negotiations on broader disputes.
However, Tehran's proposal remains conditional on Washington meeting its demands, while the United States continues to insist that concerns over Iran's nuclear programme must be addressed.
Disagreements over sanctions, the blockade on Iranian ports and mechanisms for ending hostilities across the region also remain unresolved.
The latest mediation efforts therefore present Qatar and Pakistan with a critical challenge of preventing the collapse of diplomatic contacts while securing reciprocal confidence-building measures that could pave the way for broader negotiations on Iran's nuclear programme, sanctions and regional security arrangements.
The sources' assessment that an immediate escalation is unlikely offers a potential opening for diplomacy, despite the continued exchange of threats and the absence of a comprehensive agreement between Washington and Tehran.

In France, the government is calling for local curfews amid demonstrations
Kyiv • UNN
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu instructed prefects to introduce partial curfews in areas affected by unrest. Affected businesses will receive assistance.
In France, following a weekend of protests marked by violence, the country’s Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced that he had requested the introduction of a "partial and localized" curfew. UNN reports this, citing BFM TV.
Details
Following an interministerial crisis meeting, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday, October 19, that he had asked prefects to "introduce a series of curfews" after the violence and destruction that occurred this weekend during the demonstrations.
"They will be partial; they may be very localized," he explained.
"I asked the prefects to introduce a series of curfews this evening" in order to "protect property and businesses," Sébastien Lecornu said after the interministerial meeting.
"We are dealing with a very specific type of large-scale looting. We cannot allow this to continue for so long," he said.
"The French people watching on television say: ‘There is chaos everywhere,’ but fortunately, no. We do have chaos, frankly—sorry for the expression—but it is very localized in city centers," Sébastien Lecornu assured.
"This curfew will be localized and partial. There is absolutely no question of imposing a curfew throughout Paris. That makes no sense," Sébastien Lecornu asserted, noting that he was focusing on "specific areas."
"Social partners have the right to demonstrate; the issue is finding the right balance between restoring public order—which is my absolute priority—and not infringing on freedoms," he continued.
During his remarks, Sébastien Lecornu reiterated that his "determination to restore order" was "complete." "If necessary," the government would also be ready to declare a state of emergency, he said, although for now a curfew "seems more appropriate for the situation."
To enable businesses to "restart very quickly," Sébastien Lecornu announced that partial unemployment assistance would be introduced "as early as tomorrow" for those most affected by damage and looting. "This is a measure to protect employment. In this situation, there is no question of further social unrest after the destruction we have already experienced," he added.
A special support fund will also be allocated for all affected businesses, in addition to the ongoing negotiations with insurance companies regarding the "accelerated assessment."
According to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, police made 351 arrests in the French capital on Sunday. The government announced that "at least 3,000 businesses" across the country were affected by damage or looting over the weekend.

Koretsky highlights close government alignment with president, notes top-down decision-making in wartime governance
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
14:44:39 EEST
20:44:39 KST

The Ukrainian government maintains close communication with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, with many decisions executed vertically, while the Cabinet's duty is to ensure horizontal operational implementation, Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky stated in an interview with the BBC.
According to him, under conditions of full-scale war, the Supreme Commander-in-Chief—possessing a comprehensive overview of the situation—can make decisions more rapidly, particularly within the defense sector.
"We can discuss this in various ways, but it is precisely this system of coordinates that enabled us to stand over these five years and continue fighting," the Prime Minister noted.
"Therefore, we are in very close communication, and many things operate vertically. My task is to ensure the horizontal functionality of the government, for which the Cabinet is directly responsible," Koretsky said in response to a question regarding how frequently decisions are handed down from the Office of the President.
Addressing whether he can say "no" to the President, Koretsky stated that a dialogue exists between them, and that Zelenskyy is willing to listen to alternative views.
"The President also wants to hear alternative perspectives. Ultimately, if after all discussions the President makes a decision that we act in a certain way, we proceed and execute it," he said.
Koretsky emphasized that during wartime, the primary criterion must be the rapid adoption of decisions necessary for the country's survival.
"We are at war, and there is only one criterion: we either survive as a nation and a country, or we do not," the Prime Minister declared.
He added that decisions must be made regardless of whether they are popular or unpopular, simple or complex, provided they deliver the necessary results more swiftly.

Over 95 earthquakes hit Iran in a week

Over 95 earthquakes hit Iran in a week
TEHRAN – A total of 97 earthquakes have been recorded across the country in a week from October 10 to 16, according to the seismological networks of the Institute of Geophysics of the University of Tehran.
Statistically, 85 earthquakes with magnitudes smaller than 3, 10 earthquakes with a magnitude between 3 and 4, and two earthquake with a magnitude between 4 and 5 have occurred in the country, irsc reported.
Of the total quakes, one had a magnitude of 4.2 on the Richter scale which occurred on October 16 in Kerman province.
Among the provinces of the country, Kerman experienced the highest number of earthquakes with 15, followed by Yazd with 11, Khorasan Razavi and Semnan each with 9, and Qom with 8 earthquakes.
During the same period, one earthquake hit Tehran. No earthquakes were recorded in Ardabil, Alborz, Khuzestan, Zanjan, Sistan-Baluchestan, Qom, Qazvin, Gilan, Markazi, and Hamedan provinces.
A total of 2,380 earthquakes with a magnitude of more than 2.5 on the Richter scale were recorded across the country over the past calendar year (March 2025–March 2026), according to the Seismological networks of the Institute of Geophysics of the University of Tehran, Mehr news agency reported.
Out of recorded earthquakes, 910 had a magnitude greater than 3, 130 had a magnitude greater than 4, and 15 had a magnitude greater than 5 on the Richter scale.
The Iranian plateau is located in a very seismically active region of the world and is known not only for its major catastrophic earthquakes but also for the disasters relating to natural hazards, especially earthquakes.
About 2 percent of the earthquakes in the world occur in Iran, but more than 6 percent of the victims of the world’s earthquakes during the 20th century are reported from Iranian earthquakes.

- Alperen Sengun will play for Houston Rockets, Adem Bona for Philadelphia 76ers, and Tarik Biberovic for Dallas Mavericks
The 2026-27 NBA season kicks off Tuesday with three Turkish players set to take the court in the league’s 81st season.
The opening day will feature a single game, with the Detroit Pistons hosting the Boston Celtics at Little Caesars Arena in Michigan. The game will tip off at 3pm local time (1900 GMT).
 
Three Turkish players in action
Three Turkish players will compete in the NBA this season, with Alperen Sengun playing for the Houston Rockets, Adem Bona representing the Philadelphia 76ers and Tarik Biberovic joining the Dallas Mavericks.
Two-time All-Star Sengun will enter the season aiming to lead the Rockets back to the playoffs.
Bona's 76ers will look to contend with a strengthened roster featuring LeBron James and Jaylen Brown.
Biberovic, meanwhile, will make his NBA debut with the Mavericks.
 
Sengun enters sixth NBA season
The 24-year-old Sengun, who has established himself among the NBA's top players, will begin his sixth season in the league.
He averaged 20.4 points, 8.9 rebounds, 6.2 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.1 blocks per game last season as the Rockets finished fifth in the Western Conference.
Sengun became the first Turkish player to be selected to consecutive All-Star Games last season and helped Houston reach the playoffs for the second time in his career.
 
Thunder, Spurs and Knicks among teams in spotlight
The Oklahoma City Thunder, the San Antonio Spurs and the New York Knicks are the teams to watch entering the new season with hopes to secure the championship.
The New York Knicks will begin their title defense, while the San Antonio Spurs will be led by French star Victor Wembanyama. The Oklahoma City Thunder, who have been among the league's leading teams in recent seasons, will also enter the campaign targeting a championship.
 
LeBron James enters 24th NBA season
LeBron James will begin his 24th NBA season with the Philadelphia 76ers after previously playing for the Cleveland Cavaliers, Miami Heat and Los Angeles Lakers.
The NBA's all-time leading scorer, James will extend his record for the most seasons played in the league.
The 41-year-old has won four NBA championships and has been named the NBA's Most Valuable Player four times in the regular season and four times in the Finals.
James will seek to add further records and another championship to his career in Philadelphia.

The final four playoff berths will be determined through the play-in tournament, featuring teams finishing seventh through 10th in each conference. The play-in games will be held from April 13-16.

Iran joins two-week biodiversity negotiations at COP17 in Armenia
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
11:42:40 UTC
20:42:40 KST

Iran joins two-week biodiversity negotiations at COP17 in Armenia
TEHRAN – Iran is participating in the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the Convention on Biological Diversity in Armenia with a delegation of experts and academics led by Hamid Zohrabi, deputy head of the Department of Environment.
The two-week negotiations, which began on Sunday, will be held in two stages: technical-level discussions followed by the ministerial segment.
The leaders’ summit took place last Friday, featuring an address by President Masoud Pezeshkian. It marked the first time a president of the Islamic Republic of Iran had attended a Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity.
Addressing the summit, Pezeshkian called for “peace diplomacy” to protect biodiversity, condemning the devastating environmental impact of wars of aggression as ecocide and urging the international community to establish effective, transparent and enforceable mechanisms to safeguard natural heritage during wartime.
Pezeshkian described environmental cooperation as a bridge between nations, stressing that biodiversity conservation could serve as an important pillar of “peace diplomacy.”
“In a region facing security crises stemming from the illegal and expansionist presence of powers, as well as climate change, water scarcity and ecosystem degradation, environmental cooperation can build bridges between nations,” he said.
Such cooperation, he added, can pave the way for peace and security for all, peace with nature, and a future in which human life is aligned and in harmony with the natural world.
“Today, we stand at a pivotal moment in history when biodiversity is no longer merely a scientific or environmental concern. It is also an issue of peace and security, human health, food and water security, and intergenerational justice for all the inhabitants of our planet,” Pezeshkian stressed.
“The Islamic Republic of Iran was among the first countries to recognize the legal and international significance of this issue and become a party to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD). However, Iran’s relationship with biodiversity goes far beyond its membership in an international convention.
With an ancient tradition of living in harmony with nature and an extraordinary diversity of ecosystems, species and genetic resources, Iran is the custodian of an invaluable and irreplaceable natural wealth. This heritage is the result of millions of years of evolution, natural dynamism and adaptation, and is reflected in the culture, customs, livelihoods, indigenous knowledge and historical identity of the people of this land.
Owing to its exceptional geographical location, Iran lies at the intersection of several biogeographical regions. From the Hyrcanian and Arasbaran forests to the Zagros Mountains, and from arid and desert landscapes to the coasts of the Persian Gulf, the Sea of Oman and the Caspian Sea, Iran is home to thousands of plant and animal species, as well as valuable genetic resources. These natural assets underpin the country’s ecological stability and sustainability, provide a vital foundation for water and food security and human health, strengthen resilience to natural hazards, and serve as a cornerstone of sustainable development.
Shina Ansari, the head of the Department of Environment, also addressed the meeting, saying that environmental diplomacy can become an instrument of peace diplomacy, while the relationship between biodiversity, peace, and security should be viewed as a two-way relationship.
Ansari added the link between biodiversity and peace was not merely an ethical or political issue, but a fundamental concern in environmental governance, international law, and human security.
Under the Convention on Biological Diversity, she said, the main drivers of biodiversity loss are generally understood to include land-use change, habitat destruction, pollution, unsustainable exploitation of natural resources, and climate change.
COP17 is being held From 19 to 30 October under the framework of the Convention on Biological Diversity, alongside the Twelfth meeting of the Parties to the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety (CP-MOP-12) and the Sixth meeting of the Parties to the Nagoya Protocol on Access to Genetic Resources and the Fair and Equitable Sharing of Benefits Arising from Their Utilization (NP-MOP-6).
At the 1992 United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (Earth Summit) in Rio de Janeiro, world leaders agreed on a comprehensive strategy for sustainable development aimed at ensuring a healthy and productive planet for future generations. One of the Summit's landmark achievements was the adoption of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).
Signed by the vast majority of the world's countries, the Convention establishes commitments to conserve the foundations of the Earth's ecosystems while pursuing economic development. Its objectives are the conservation of biological diversity, the sustainable use of its components, and the fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising from the utilization of genetic resources. These objectives are pursued through appropriate access to genetic resources, the transfer of relevant technologies—taking into account all rights over those resources and technologies—and the provision of adequate financial resources, in accordance with the Convention's provisions.

Russia’s Budget Deficit Hits $61B, Exceeding Full-Year Plan by 37%
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
11:41:22 UTC
20:41:22 KST

- Category
- World
Russia’s Budget Deficit Hits $61B, Exceeding Full-Year Plan by 37%
Russia’s federal budget deficit reached $61.08 billion in the first nine months of 2026, exceeding the Kremlin’s original full-year target by 37%, Ukraine’s Foreign Intelligence Service reported on October 18.
The January–September shortfall amounted to 5.186 trillion rubles, or 2.2% of GDP, compared with the government’s initial annual target of $44.59 billion, or 1.6% of GDP.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
In September, Russia’s Finance Ministry raised its full-year deficit forecast to $86.51 billion, equivalent to 7.345 trillion rubles or 3.2% of GDP, the intelligence service reported.
Federal spending increased 14.5% year-on-year during the first nine months, reaching $410.19 billion. Revenue rose more slowly, by 10%, to $349.10 billion.
Russia’s oil and gas revenues fell 17.2% over the same period to $64.44 billion, according to the Ukrainian intelligence assessment.
Non-oil and gas revenues increased 18.8% to $284.66 billion, while value-added tax receipts rose 27.4% to $158.62 billion.
The Foreign Intelligence Service noted that the additional tax revenue was not enough to offset falling oil and gas income and rising government expenditure.
Russia is therefore spending more than it collects and must cover the gap through accumulated reserves or borrowing, the agency stated.
It added that drawing down funds held in government accounts reduces the resources available for future spending. In the near term, Moscow could be forced to seek additional revenue through higher taxes, increase borrowing, or cut budget expenditure.
The widening deficit is already pushing Moscow toward higher taxes. In September, Russia prepared measures expected to raise nearly $44 billion from individuals and businesses through 2029, including higher taxes on passive income and new levies on metals, mining, and other industries as war spending continues to rise.

Trump Eases Russia Sanctions “for Peace” as Zelenskyy Warns of Forced Ukraine Capitulation
US President Donald Trump has defended his decision to suspend sanctions against Russia as an effort to preserve peace negotiations, even as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warns that Washington’s recent actions increasingly resemble pressure on Kyiv to capitulate to Moscow.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to BBC News on October 19, Trump blocked several sanctions against Russia just two days before they were scheduled to take effect, arguing that imposing additional restrictions could drive Moscow away from negotiations.
“I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that he did not want to “do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table”.
The decision effectively delayed sanctions previously approved by the US Congress and signed into law in September. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the move as a 60-day suspension intended to assess the potential impact of the restrictions on the American and global economies.
Moscow welcomed the decision. Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev called it “an important and truly historic moment,” claiming the sanctions would have caused serious damage to the US and global markets.
While the Trump administration presents the suspension as a diplomatic measure, Zelenskyy has raised concerns that Washington’s broader approach could leave Ukraine facing increasing pressure to accept Russian demands.
In an interview with Bloomberg on October 18, Zelenskyy said recent US decisions appeared to be pushing Ukraine toward surrender. “I believe steps were taken to convince Ukraine to capitulate,” Zelenskyy said.
The Ukrainian president clarified that he was describing the apparent consequences of Washington’s actions rather than accusing American officials of deliberately seeking Ukraine’s surrender.
“I don’t want to think that our American partners believe the war can be ended faster at Ukraine’s expense. But that is what it looks like,” he added.
His concerns extend beyond sanctions policy. Zelenskyy cited restrictions on Starlink satellite connectivity, delays in deliveries of Patriot interceptor missiles already purchased by Ukraine, and interruptions in intelligence sharing as examples of decisions affecting Kyiv’s ability to defend itself against Russian attacks.
Trump has rejected accusations that Washington deliberately restricted Starlink services or stopped sharing defense intelligence with Ukraine.
The disagreement has also deepened over Washington’s decision to purchase Russian diesel amid rising energy prices linked to the war involving Iran.
Zelenskyy criticized the arrangement, arguing that American purchases of Russian fuel would effectively contribute revenue to Moscow while its forces continue attacking Ukraine.
Despite international sanctions, Russia remains a major oil exporter. According to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air, China purchases approximately half of Russia’s crude exports, while India accounts for around 37%.
Trump has also accused Zelenskyy of obstructing negotiations, claiming that the Ukrainian president “doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did”.
Zelenskyy, meanwhile, has maintained that Russia must face sustained international pressure to reach an agreement that does not come at the expense of Ukraine’s sovereignty.
Zelenskyy also said that recent US decisions, including restrictions on military assistance and Starlink connectivity, appeared to be aimed at pressuring Ukraine into capitulation to Russia.
“I believe steps were taken to convince Ukraine to capitulate,” Zelenskyy told Bloomberg, while clarifying that he did not necessarily believe Washington intended that outcome.
Zelenskyy also said the US is currently supplying Ukraine with just 12 Patriot interceptor missiles per month, roughly four times fewer than under the Biden administration, while delaying approval for additional weapons Kyiv has already paid for.

Swiss army rejected US tech firm Palantir on five occasions
In recent years, the Swiss army has considered collaborating with Palantir five times but rejected overtures from the controversial United States technology company each time.
This is shown by research conducted by the online magazine Republik and the research collective WAV. According to the research, one reason was concern about the security of confidential data.
Palantir is among the most powerful and controversial companies in the world. Thanks to its artificial intelligence model, capable of rapidly processing large amounts of data, it promises real-time solutions to the most complex and sensitive problems, including those on the battlefield.
The US tech company’s product range includes software for preventing terrorist attacks and identifying military targets. Palantir’s clients include governments, armies, and intelligence agencies of various countries. But not in Switzerland. According to research by Republik and WAV, the Swiss army has rejected cooperation with Palantir five times.
More
Why Palantir is becoming a risky bet for Switzerland
“We not only discovered these five contacts between experts from the Swiss army, but also the reasons why the cooperation was rejected,” Balz Oertli, one of the journalists involved in the Palantir investigation, told Swiss public broadcaster (RSI). “In three of the five cases, it was the lack of control over the data that led to the rejection.”
For the army experts, it was a question of sovereignty in handling confidential information. “They obviously didn’t trust Palantir enough,” Oertli concludes.
Parliament ot debate ban
The journalistic investigation into Palantir was conducted at the European level through a collaboration between various media outlets. It revealed a contract volume of €1.44 billion for Palantir in Europe. The tech company generates the majority of its total revenue of approximately €4 billion in the US.
“Nevertheless, the lack of cooperation with the Swiss army is significant,” Oertli added. “Switzerland would certainly have been a very good customer.” It is neutral and outside of NATO. Furthermore, its army is comparable in size to other potential customers. The various rejections are therefore “a problem for Palantir.”
The US corporation can, however, continue to offer its services in Switzerland. The Federal Department of Defence, headed by Martin Pfister, has not yet made a fundamental decision that would preclude cooperation.
However, this could become an issue in parliament. A parliamentary initiative has been submitted by the Green Party calling for a ban on contracts with foreign providers of such services – citing concerns about the transparency and security of confidential data, as expressed by army specialists.

Putin Wants Trump and Xi to Decide Ukraine’s Future at Three-Way Summit in China, WSJ Reports
Russian leader Vladimir Putin has proposed holding a trilateral summit with US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in November to discuss the war in Ukraine and pursue a potential settlement favorable to Moscow, according to Suspilne on October 19, citing The Wall Street Journal.
The proposed meeting would take place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, scheduled for November 18–19 in Shenzhen, China, the newspaper reported.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to one source, Putin raised the proposal during a phone conversation with Trump on October 9, during which the two leaders reportedly reached an agreement on US purchases of Russian diesel fuel and assistance in facilitating its sales on international markets.
Peskov confirmed that discussions about a possible trilateral meeting were underway but stressed that neither the format nor the agenda had been finalized.
However, a senior US official said Trump had not agreed to participate in the proposed summit. The official suggested that the American president might nevertheless be receptive to the idea, given his stated commitment to fulfilling his campaign promise to resolve the war in Ukraine.
Meanwhile, Russian officials have reportedly presented the proposal to Beijing through diplomatic channels. According to sources cited by the newspaper, Chinese representatives indicated they would not oppose the meeting if Trump supported the initiative.
According to Suspilne, for Moscow, the proposed summit represents an opportunity to reinforce Russia’s position among the world's major powers while potentially shaping negotiations over Ukraine without direct European participation.
The Kremlin views Europe as a major obstacle to achieving its objectives in Ukraine, making a trilateral format involving Washington and Beijing particularly attractive to Moscow, the outlet reported.
The potential summit could also strengthen Xi’s efforts to position China as an influential diplomatic mediator, particularly if Beijing hosts discussions involving the leaders of the United States and Russia.
However, the proposed format presents diplomatic challenges for China, whose officials reportedly fear that discussions about Ukraine could overshadow Beijing’s broader objectives for the APEC summit.
According to the report, Chinese authorities are concerned that the war in Ukraine, which they regard as a secondary geopolitical issue in the context of the summit, could divert attention from their plans to showcase China's regional influence.
A trilateral meeting could also draw Beijing more directly into diplomatic efforts surrounding the war and provoke criticism from European governments already concerned about China's increasingly close relationship with Moscow.
The discussions come amid renewed debate over Washington’s approach to pressuring Russia into negotiations, particularly following Trump's decision to delay additional sanctions against Moscow.
According to BBC News on October 19, the US president blocked several sanctions targeting Russia just two days before they were scheduled to take effect, arguing that further economic restrictions could jeopardize ongoing peace efforts.
Trump defended the decision as necessary to preserve the possibility of a negotiated settlement. Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed concern that Washington’s recent actions increasingly appeared to place pressure on Kyiv to accept Moscow’s demands rather than intensify pressure on Russia.

Russia Caught Shipping Weapons and Suspected Undercover Spies to Africa Aboard Civilian Vessels
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
11:41:09 UTC
20:41:09 KST

- Category
- World
Russia Caught Shipping Weapons and Suspected Undercover Spies to Africa Aboard Civilian Vessels
Russia has been using civilian cargo ships to transport military equipment and suspected undercover intelligence operatives to Africa, with investigators identifying 28 passengers believed to have traveled under fabricated identities aboard vessels carrying supplies for Russian military operations on the continent.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to a joint investigation published on October 19 by the Dossier Center, Follow the Money, Süddeutsche Zeitung, Danwatch, and Delfi, the suspected operatives traveled aboard seven Russian cargo vessels transporting military equipment primarily intended for Russia’s Africa Corps, a Defense Ministry-controlled formation that replaced the Wagner mercenary group.
Journalists identified 28 passengers whose names, dates of birth, and identity document numbers could not be found in publicly available records or leaked databases. A source within European intelligence services suggested that the individuals were likely Russian intelligence personnel operating under cover identities.
The investigation found that the passengers used Russian passports without biometric chips. Several documents differed only in their final digits, while two carried consecutive numbers, suggesting they may have been issued together as part of a coordinated operation.
Former Danish intelligence officer Stig Wæver assessed that the documents displayed characteristics associated with passports used in intelligence operations. Analysts at US-based security research organization C4ADS also concluded that the passengers’ personal information appeared to have been fabricated.
One of the shipments involved the Russian cargo vessel Sabetta, which arrived at the port of Conakry, Guinea, on March 19. The ship reportedly delivered approximately 50 military and support vehicles, including armored vehicles and fuel tankers.
The equipment was subsequently transported overland to Mali, where Russia’s Africa Corps maintains a military presence. Four passengers aboard Sabetta had identity details that investigators could not verify through other available records.
The vessel is owned by Severny Proekt, a Russian company involved in state defense contracts and special projects for the state nuclear corporation Rosatom.
The investigation also identified three roll-on/roll-off vessels—Adler, Ascalon, and Baltic Leader—operated by MG-Flot, a Russian shipping company sanctioned by the United States and European Union over activities linked to Iran and supplies supporting Russian drone production.
Three additional cargo ships—Mikhail Britnev, Mys Zhelaniya, and Siyanie Severa—were also identified as part of the maritime network. Siyanie Severa had previously transported grain from temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories.
According to the investigation, the vessels frequently switched off their Automatic Identification System (AIS) transponders during voyages to Africa, making their movements more difficult to track.
A source within a European intelligence agency suggested that Russia may have deployed personnel from the Federal Security Service (FSB) or military intelligence agency (GRU) to accompany the shipments because of the sensitive military cargo.
Michelle Bockmann, a senior analyst at maritime intelligence company Windward, suggested that the suspected intelligence operatives could have been tasked with monitoring crews and preventing vessels from complying with potential orders to stop issued by European authorities.
Russia’s expanding military presence in Africa has also drawn Ukrainian involvement. According to CNN on September 12, approximately 15 Ukrainian drone specialists have been operating in Mali, providing training and operational support to local forces fighting Russia’s Africa Corps.
Ukrainian personnel have also reportedly conducted drone operations in Sudan and Libya, targeting Russian-linked military and maritime activities.

IN BRIEF: What we know about protests in Europe
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
11:39:07 UTC
20:39:07 KST

MOSCOW, October 19. /TASS/. French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez submitted his resignation on Monday, but President Emmanuel Macron rejected it, the BFMTV channel reported.
In Italy, almost 200 people have been detained during several days of unrest, Sky TG24 reported.
TASS has compiled the main details about the situation in European countries.
Protests in France
- Large-scale demonstrations against rising fuel prices and the declining purchasing power of the population took place in Paris and across France on Saturday.
- According to organizers, 800,000 people took to the streets, while the Interior Ministry put the number at 550,000, double the figure estimated by analysts at security agencies.
- In a number of cities, the protests turned into riots and clashes with police.
- French police have detained 2,397 people during the large-scale protests, AFP reported, citing data from the Interior Ministry.
- As many as 997 police and gendarmerie officers were injured in clashes, including seven who sustained serious injuries, the Interior Ministry said.
Response from French authorities
- French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez stated that the clampdown on all participants in pogroms and looting would continue.
- French President Emmanuel Macron described the situation amid the unrest that has swept across the country as extremely challenging.
- He called the October 17 events "unbridled violence," blaming them on "factious groups from the ultra-left."
- Macron demanded that the government draw lessons from the developments and do everything to prevent a repetition of what happened.
- The French leader also demanded that all political parties and trade unions "unequivocally condemn any violence" and urged calm.
- According to Macron, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu will convene a meeting with their representatives in the next few days to establish "a clear and publicly expressed position."
- Ahead of the presidential election scheduled for next spring, Macron said, "debates should be held with political parties taking part but not through street violence."
- On October 19, Nunez submitted his resignation amid protests in the republic, but Macron rejected it, BFMTV reported.
- At the same time, the head of state highlighted "the failures in planning and intelligence that led to the violence," the TV channel said.
- According to BFMTV, Macron asked Nunez to "put in place new operational methods for security forces" in their fight against hooligans.
Statements from French opposition
- Leader of the National Rally party Jordan Bardella described the unrest in the country as "a humiliation for France" and called on Macron to step down.
- Presidential candidate for the 2027 election Jean-Luc Melenchon, leader of La France Insoumise (LFI), blamed Macron for the violence.
- The authorities had underestimated the scale of the protests and were unprepared for them, he argued.
Situation in Italy
- Demonstrations against the policies pursued by Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni began on October 16, with student marches held in many cities across the country.
- Protests continued on October 17, when members of the country’s largest trade union, the Italian General Confederation of Labor, joined the youth protests.
- Around 5,000 people have taken to the streets in Milan, 3,000 others in Turin, another 2,000 in Bologna, 600 more in Brescia and 800 others in Bergamo, according to the latest information.
- Meloni said taking part in demonstrations was the right of Italians but condemned the unrest.
- Almost 200 people were detained during several days of unrest in Italy, Sky TG24 reported.
- According to the television channel, 197 people were detained following clashes in Bergamo, Bologna, and Turin, including 12 minors and six foreigners.
- As many as 141 police officers have been reported injured.
Situation in Albania
- The unrest in Tirana broke out on October 13, during a student protest outside the Ministry of Education building.
- Protesters have been demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama.
- Sali Berisha, chairman of Albania’s leading opposition Democratic Party, voiced his support for the protests.
- Earlier, Rama said a drone carrying an explosive had been neutralized not far from his residence in Tirana, claiming that protests in the country were "inspired from abroad."
- Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova called on the Albanian head of government not to transfer responsibility for the unrest in the country to Russia or Iran.
- Before clashes erupted in Tirana, anti-government rallies had been held for more than 130 days over a luxury tourism development the authorities are promoting in the nature preserve of Vjosa-Narta on the republic’s Adriatic coast.
- Earlier, Albania’s Special Anti-Corruption Structure launched a probe into amendments to the status of this national park that Affinity Partners, the investment firm owned by US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, wants to turn into an eco-resort.
- The project threatens the uninhabited island of Sazan in southern Albania and several hundred hectares of protected landscape there.
Russia’s stance
- Nobody takes seriously any longer absurd accusations of Russia’s involvement in unrest in Europe against Russia, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.
- The EU’s accusations show how disrespectful the bloc is toward its own citizens, Zakharova noted.
- She also posted a video of protests in a number of European countries on her Telegram channel commenting on Europe under attack.
- The video begins with European politicians, including French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, discussing the alleged threat from Russia.
- Their remarks are followed by footage of riots and pogroms in France, Italy and Albania, with the caption "Are those Russians?"
- The final shots of the video show the words "No, it is Europeans who are attacking Europe aka the ‘garden’" as a response to that question.

====================================================================================================

Israel’s AI propaganda was built to silence Palestinians. Now it targets voters at home.
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
11:36:46 UTC
20:36:46 KST

Israel’s first election advertisement to be banned for undisclosed use of artificial intelligence presented a scene of peace. In the fabricated video, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot embraces Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas.
The footage was produced by Bezalel Smotrich’s far-right Religious Zionism party to frighten voters with the suggestion that Eisenkot might reconcile with the Palestinians.
The irony is difficult to miss. A synthetic image of coexistence was deployed as a political threat by a movement whose ministers have openly advocated annexation, displacement and the destruction of Palestinian life.
Yet the fake video is only the visible edge of a much larger system.
As Israel approaches crucial national elections, AI is not simply being used to invent images. It is being used to manufacture voters, infiltrate private conversations, harvest personal information, and quietly shape what people believe is public opinion.
The Economist reports that Israeli technology companies have developed swarms of bots that masquerade as human voters, influence online conversations and distort informal polls.
More sophisticated AI avatars can have telephone numbers and even credit cards, letting them join WhatsApp groups and act like real people.
Political campaigns can combine information gathered through chatbots with commercial data on purchases, searches, viewing habits, and location, then tailor advertisements, messages, and lifelike robocalls to individual voters.
This should alarm anyone concerned with democracy. But there is a danger in telling the story as though Israel has suddenly discovered a menacing technology on the eve of its own election.
The machinery did not appear from nowhere. It was developed, funded and normalised through years of information warfare directed at Palestinians, Arabs and Western publics. What is new is not the weapon. It is the identity of some of its targets.
Money poured into Hasbara
Since October 2023, Israel has treated public opinion as another front in its genocidal war on Gaza.
Its government has poured extraordinary sums into hasbara, the state’s public diplomacy and influence apparatus.
Its 2025 allocation of roughly $150 million was already a dramatic expansion.
The 2026 budget reportedly raised that figure to about $730 million. An investigation by the Quincy Institute concluded that direct Israeli government spending on public diplomacy since October 2023 had exceeded $1 billion.
That money does more than purchase conventional advertising.
In 2024, OpenAI exposed an Israel-based influence operation it called ‘Zero Zeno’. The network, operated by the Israeli political marketing firm STOIC, used AI to generate articles, comments and fabricated online personas across Facebook, Instagram, X, YouTube and websites posing as independent organisations.
Its material attacked UNRWA, portrayed pro-Palestinian university protesters as “supporters of terrorism” and targeted audiences in the United States, Canada and elsewhere. Reporting at the time linked the wider campaign to Israel’s Ministry of Diaspora Affairs, which denied involvement.
The ambition has since become even more brazen. A 2026 investigation revealed that an apparently fictitious American think tank, the Hanover Institute for Public Policy, had published more than 560,000 words in nine days.
Its reports were dressed as neutral, sourced research on questions such as whether Israel was committing genocide, starving Palestinians or torturing prisoners.
The site was part of an Israeli-government-funded campaign designed to influence what AI chatbots tell users. One contract explicitly referred to delivering ‘GPT framing results’ in chatbot conversations.
This is more insidious than a clumsy deepfake. A false video can be identified, labelled and removed. But when thousands of synthetic accounts, pseudo-academic reports and engineered search results flood the information environment, propaganda begins to resemble consensus.
A user asking an apparently neutral chatbot about Gaza may never know that some of the material shaping its answer was created by a foreign government seeking to obscure its own conduct.
A manipulation apparatus
For Palestinians, this is not an abstract debate about technological ethics. The manipulation of information accompanies the destruction of lives.
While Palestinians document children killed, hospitals attacked, families starved and entire neighbourhoods erased, an immensely funded apparatus works to dispute the evidence, smear the witnesses and recast demands for accountability as “extremism” or “anti-Semitism”.
AI allows that apparatus to operate at a scale no team of human propagandists could match.
It also helps explain a familiar distortion in Western debate.
Palestinian voices are routinely treated as interested, emotional or unreliable, while Israeli state claims are repeated as the default account even when they later collapse under scrutiny.
Digital influence operations exploit that imbalance. They do not need to convince everyone. They only need to create enough noise, doubt, and artificial agreement to delay political action while facts on the ground become irreversible.
Now the same culture of manipulation is turning inward. Netanyahu and his allies have spent years building databases and election technology, while opposition-linked figures in Israel’s powerful tech sector are reportedly preparing to fight with similar tools.
The problem therefore cannot be reduced to one party or one politician. Once covert persuasion becomes an accepted instrument of statecraft, it does not remain neatly confined to foreign audiences.
A system designed to impersonate citizens abroad will eventually impersonate citizens at home.
There is another bitter contradiction.
Israeli institutions are now discussing safeguards to protect Israeli voters from AI-generated deception, yet there has been little comparable concern for the millions of people abroad whose politics have already been targeted—or for Palestinians whose reality these campaigns were built to erase.
Democracy cannot mean defending Israeli citizens from manipulation while accepting the covert manipulation of Americans, Europeans and Arabs as legitimate public diplomacy.
Nor should governments in London, Washington or Brussels treat this solely as an Israeli election story.
Foreign interference does not become benign because it comes from an ally. If Russia, China or Iran financed fake American organisations, synthetic citizens and campaigns intended to alter what chatbots tell voters, Western officials would describe it as a threat to national security.
Israel should not receive an exemption from standards applied to everyone else.
‘Profiled, targeted and manipulated’
The lesson is larger than Netanyahu. Governments must require full disclosure of state-funded digital campaigns, enforce foreign-agent and data-protection laws, compel technology companies to expose coordinated inauthentic networks and create transparency around efforts to manipulate AI training and retrieval systems.
Political parties should be prohibited from deploying synthetic identities or using covertly harvested personal data to suppress or redirect voters.
But regulation alone will not answer the moral question. Israel’s influence machine exists because its leaders believe the problem is not what the state has done to Palestinians, but that the world has seen too much of it.
No algorithm can make mass killing humane, occupation democratic or starvation defensible. The more public opinion turns against these policies, the more money and technology are spent trying to correct the public rather than the policy.
Israel’s AI propaganda apparatus is now coming home. The danger to Israeli voters is real, but Palestinians have lived for years with the consequences of the worldview that produced it: that people can be profiled, targeted and manipulated; that inconvenient truths can be buried beneath manufactured narratives; and that technology can solve a political crisis created by domination.
A weapon does not become objectionable only when those who built it discover that it can be aimed at them.

On Iran, Israel’s opposition is even more hawkish than Netanyahu
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
11:35:52 UTC
20:35:52 KST

On Iran, Israel’s opposition is even more hawkish than Netanyahu
In the rest of the world, the Israeli PM is often blamed for the Iran war. His opponents say he hasn’t been tough enough with Tehran.
When Israel launched a sweeping military assault on Iran with the United States in February, the Israeli government enjoyed overwhelming support from the Jewish Israeli public.
Opposition parties lent their support to the army and backed the audacious step. Enmity towards the government in Iran is an issue mainstream Zionist parties agree on.
Then in June, Israel’s role in the confrontation halted abruptly with an announcement from US President Donald Trump, who said Iran and Israel had agreed to stop attacking each other.
That announcement – and Netanyahu’s decision to abide by it at the time – were unpopular in Israel. According to the Israel Democracy Institute, 65 to 70 percent of Jewish Israelis believe that stopping the war did not serve Israel’s national security interests.
As Israelis prepare to vote in national elections on October 27, Iran remains an important election issue for many. Opposition parties present Iran as an example of what they say are Netanyahu’s many failures. They promise to reset security and foreign policy if they’re elected.
The frontrunner, Gadi Eisenkot, says the conflict is unfinished. While saying that a change in Iran’s government was an unrealistic goal, Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu of doing little to dismantle Iran’s nuclear programme. In September at the inauguration of his new party, Yashar, Eisenkot told supporters: “Ultimately, it must end in the destruction or dismantling of the Iranian nuclear programme, a goal not yet achieved with 440kg [970lb] of highly enriched uranium already there, which could quickly be turned into several nuclear devices.”
Former Prime Minister Yair Lapid, who is now the head of the opposition in the Knesset, accuses Netanyahu of a strategic failure. He recently told the Atlantic Council that toppling the administration in Tehran is a realistic objective that requires a military escalation: “What Israel should do or the alliance should do is bomb all the energy facilities, especially on Kharg Island, but other places as well in order to make sure that the Iranian economy is demolished. And the reason is that it’s the only thing that will overturn the regime.”
Bombing this civilian infrastructure was actually something Netanyahu had lobbied for himself. An international outcry about such bombings likely constituting war crimes and Trump’s refusal to offer backing put the brakes on the plan.
Naftali Bennett, another former prime minister, says Israel must ensure its military dominance over the entire region. For Bennett, toppling the government in Iran and crushing it is a must. But he says that is not enough. The right-wing politician calls Qatar an “enemy” and says Turkiye is “the new Iran”, going as far as saying that military confrontation with the NATO member was inevitable.
“We will build an alliance of moderate forces in the region against the Islamist forces, against Iran, against Qatar, Turkiye and all the radical forces. We will take proactive actions to shape the region,” Bennett recently told supporters.
Eisenkot and other opposition leaders do not rule out renewed confrontations. They focus on their confidence in the military and security establishment in assessing the dangers and dealing with them appropriately.
But opposition leaders have voiced concern that Netanyahu might resort to military escalation before the elections to tilt the balance in his favour or even disrupt them altogether – even though the prime minister said last week that he did not plan to attack Iran before the vote.
Those fears were elevated after Netanyahu posted a video from the Tel Nof Airbase warning that Israel’s enemies might attack before the elections. Other news reports said Netanyahu has shared intelligence on new threats from Iran with the US president.
Netanyahu was quickly rebuked by opposition leaders, who accused him of “political fearmongering”.
Lapid openly questioned Netanyahu’s motives. Lapid also accused him of using the Israeli military and bases as “backdrops” for election campaign videos.
Ultimately, most Israeli opposition parties and leaders aren’t opposed to war with Iran, and many are in fact even more hawkish in their approach towards Tehran than Netanyahu. They just don’t want a new military escalation before the elections.

Israel to Supply PULS Systems and EXTRA-MR Missiles to Unnamed European Country
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
11:35:24 UTC
20:35:24 KST

Israeli company Elbit Systems has signed a contract worth approximately $235 million to supply EXTRA-MR missiles and PULS multiple launch rocket systems to a European country.
The developer’s press service reported the deal.
The contract is scheduled to be completed over three years.
Under the agreement, Elbit Systems will supply EXTRA-MR medium-range missiles, PULS launchers, associated artillery platforms, and a logistics support package.
EXTRA-MR is a precision-guided missile designed to effectively engage high-value targets at ranges of up to 80 km. It is fully integrated with PULS launchers and existing C4I systems.
The development of the PULS (Precise & Universal Launching System) began with the Lynx rocket artillery system, developed by Israel Military Industries, which was later acquired by Elbit Systems. Israeli engineers sought to create a universal, modular platform that could launch a wide range of munitions without extensive technical modifications.
The system’s key conceptual feature is its use of a container-based design. PULS is equipped with two standardized transport-launch containers, each loaded with a specific missile type based on mission requirements, ranging from unguided rockets to precision-guided ballistic and cruise missiles.
The artillery system can employ AccuLAR-122 rockets (18 rockets per launch pod, with a range of up to 35 km), AccuLAR-160 rockets (10 rockets, with a range of up to 40 km), EXTRA missiles (4 missiles, with a range of up to 150 km), as well as Predator Hawk ballistic missiles (2 missiles, with a range of up to 300 km).
The EXTRA (Extended Range Artillery) missile has a 306 mm caliber, a length of about 4.7 meters, and a total weight of nearly 450 kg. It carries either a high-explosive fragmentation warhead or a penetrating warhead weighing up to 120 kg.
The high accuracy of the EXTRA and EXTRA-MR missiles is achieved through a combined guidance system that integrates GPS satellite navigation with an inertial navigation system, providing a circular error probable of less than 10 meters at maximum firing range.
The PULS launcher can be mounted on a variety of wheeled chassis with a payload capacity of 10 tonnes or more, including those manufactured by Tatra, MAN, and Scania. The system can transition from march configuration to combat-ready position in less than three minutes.
PULS’s versatility and advanced technical capabilities have made it highly sought after on the international market. In addition to the Israel Defense Forces, where it is in service under the designation Lahav, the system and its variants have been selected by the Netherlands, Denmark, Germany (MARS 3), and several other NATO and Middle Eastern countries.

Border police won’t publish Schiphol e-gate investigation
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
11:34:37 UTC
20:34:37 KST

Border police won’t publish Schiphol e-gate investigation
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
Hundreds of people missed their flights and thousands more faced long delays at Schiphol on Sunday after all 78 of the airport’s automatic passport gates went down at around 6am.
The Royal Marechaussee, the military police force responsible for border checks, said the outage was caused by an IT malfunction and that there was “no indication whatsoever” of a cyberattack.
The exact cause is still being investigated, but the results will not be made public, Marechaussee head of press, Major Mike Hofman, told Dutch News.
“For operational reasons, we do not comment regarding the further configuration, operation and technical details of our systems,” he said.
With the e-gates down, everyone flying to or from a country outside the Schengen area had to be checked manually by hand, including passengers in transit. The Marechaussee opened every desk and carried out less thorough checks to keep the queues moving.
Passengers waited an hour on average, and some waited up to an hour and a half, Schiphol officials said. The gates were working again by around 3pm.
KLM held departures where possible, and Transavia said it would be flexible with rebookings. A claims specialist told the Telegraaf the number of people affected in some way could run into the tens of thousands.
Few are likely to receive compensation, experts told the paper, because the outage will probably count as force majeure since the e-gates are run by the Marechaussee, not the airlines. The Marechaussee said travellers who missed their flights should contact their airline.
The outage happened during one of the busiest weekends of the autumn, as the one-week October school holiday began in the middle and south of the country and ended in the north. The Amsterdam marathon on Sunday also attracted thousands of runners to the city from all over the world.

TBILISI, October 19. /TASS/. Georgian fig deliveries to Russia stood at 948.4 metric tons in September 2026, marking a record-breaking monthly high, according to data from the Georgian national statistical service reviewed by TASS.
According to the authority, exports of fresh or dried figs from Georgia to Russia in September reached 948.4 metric tons valued at $1.3 mln, which is 1.7 times higher than the figure of September of last year. The previous record for fig shipments to Russia was set in August 2025 and amounted to 916.6 metric tons.
In total, since July, the start of the fig ripening season, Georgia has exported 1,800 metric tons to Russia valued at $2.4 mln. Apart from Russia, this commodity was purchased from Georgia in minor quantities by Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan (18 metric tons each), and Armenia (2.5 metric tons).
